author: Ifmyante
text:
Okay

so I got quite lost in that video!

But let me respond to what I think I understood of it.

If a FL is visible in a certain timeframe, then it is a FL on that TF.

If it's the kink of the top or bottom of an higher TF FL, it becomes significant in the HTF.

My definition of a BSZ differs from your video.

For me, a BSZ is the area beyond two or more horizontally aligned
highs/lows, set to trick retailers into believing the S/R is strong, and
 trading it with stops beyond.

A single H/L can be a trap too, but it's set to catch the stops of SD traders

author: Edge
text:
Hi Bobby,

I hope you dont mind. Here is my take on the BSZ. IF, can correct me. I
 may have posted this before so please forgive me for being repetitious.
 Lets take the below scenario for example.

I know its only a diagram (ignore the terrible R), but sometimes they
work better for the concepts before applying to the charts.

We have a BSZ, but we also have a engulf into space. The problem is
though we dont know if the engulf is reacting the OF from A. (eg: would
like to see A retested before the engulf). So for me in this case, there
 would be a opportunity for a BSZ trade, as I am not relying on PA.

the BSZ is a area for the ITs to get their liquidity. Its the FL where
we are looking to trade. not the BSZ itself. Its just another trap. the
BSZ itself is a indication the ITs are tricking and creating liquidity
for themselves before price turns We have to ask ourselves if we dont
have a opportunity for ITs to get their liquidity on the approach we
should be cautious.

The BSZ is often a quick scalp with lower R (not all the time).
Furthermore, because we are not relying on the EG but rather the trap
(ie: two or more highs/lows) it seems like a TT which may also have a
lower win rate than a PA trade. I also like to see clean orders in the
FL we are leaning on.

In regards to your point in your question to IF , for me I like to look
for a good FL (has to be a UFL/LFL for me and confluence with a LS),
having multiple highs/lows lining up prior to the FL (not within the FL
on that scale but before the FL in no mans land). entry at a nice set of
 orders within the FL, SL beyond whole FL and just ride it back to the
kink of the BSZ.

It may not directly go to your question but I hope it helps. IF/H/M you
know the deal, should I be wrong please give me a kick in the arse.

text:
Ifmyante wrote: I've tried many
many many disciplines in my life, and as soon as I had one mastered, I
lost interest and moved on to learn the next.

To be honest, I'm running out of new things to try.

Hi IF

What else did you study in the past and mastered? I hope you don't mind me asking this question.

I really want to understand how you figured out the market. Before I got
 to to RTM, I have read other forms of technical analysis: indicators,
candlesticks, and elliott waves (this one really got me thrilled. I was
like I have finally found the holy grail but it was too subjective for
me) and fundamental analysis. Aside from reading about pumping and
dumping stocks, the idea of price movement not being random to the
extent being taught in RTM has never crossed my mind. More so that the
rationale behind the price movement are the ITs. Thinking of this makes
me think of you as someone from the FBI or CIA or maybe Sherlock Holmes
to be able to reverse engineer the market. Honestly, I believe I am
jealous of the qualities that you possess which led you to master not
only trading but also the other disciplines. Nonetheless, I wish you the
 best. :) (Please answer my questions regarding the disciplines you've
master.)

author: Ifmyante
text:
I should imagine that what I mastered is less important than how I
mastered them, and I'm not entirely certain I can explain how it's done

All I know is that I question everything. Absolutely EVERYTHING.

I know that if a human can do something, I can do it too.

I don't travel in groups. I always make my own path.

I try not to bother my brain too much, as it's much smarter than I am,
and is always busy working out how everything I've ever learned
correlates to everything else I've ever learned.

Nobody should ever want to be like me! I live in a world of endless
possibilities, and can't for the life of me focus on any one of them!
